content_blocks.body:
The most widely cited estimate in health equity work: clinical care accounts for approximately 10–20% of health outcomes. The remaining 80–90% is shaped by social and economic factors, health behaviors, and environment.

This doesn't mean health care doesn't matter — it does, especially in acute crisis. But it does mean that a health system laser-focused on clinical quality while ignoring where patients live, work, eat, and breathe is optimizing the wrong variable.
content_blocks.heading: 30% clinical care, 70% everything else

items.body: Educational attainment is one of the strongest predictors of health. More education → higher income, better jobs, better health literacy, longer life.
items.title: Education access & quality

items.body: Income, employment, food security, housing stability. Poverty is a powerful health risk factor — both through material deprivation and chronic stress.
items.title: Economic stability

items.body: Social support, discrimination, community cohesion, civic participation. Social isolation is comparable to smoking 15 cigarettes/day for health impact.
items.title: Social & community context

items.body: Insurance coverage, geographic access to providers, quality of care received, health literacy, and trust in health care systems.
items.title: Health care access & quality

items.body: Housing quality, air and water quality, access to healthy food, walkability, safety. ZIP code predicts health better than genetic code.
